conclusions: Neither vc23 candidate demonstrates an improvement over vc22_both in full API: 25.8416 and 25.8799 ms versus 25.6810 ms.

Maxstate CUPTI median is slightly lower (23.9872 versus 24.1135 ms), but per-trial differences have mixed signs and core/full API medians do not improve. Raw API trials are unavailable; no confidence interval or repeatable small regression is inferred.
Cached-bias CUPTI median is essentially level (24.1250 versus 24.1135 ms). This does not establish a win.
All custom candidates report 168 registers, zero local bytes, 41088 shared bytes and predicted three resident blocks. These results do not show an occupancy or spill regression.
The vc22_both gain reproduces: full API 25.6810 versus vc16 27.2146 and original Sage 26.6324 ms. vc22_both is faster in each corresponding CUPTI trial as well.
Initial stage tables and one-off traces measure default vc15, not the max-state candidates. Compare candidate timings within their own measurement regime.
Retain vc22_both as the experimental baseline; do not promote vc23. Public default remains vc15. Explicit kernel_mode="vc22_both", v_smooth=False selects the measured winner.
Hypothesis, not measured stall attribution: skipping two scalar exponentials and bias FMAs may save little critical-path time while earlier vote/predicate/state dependencies offset the savings.
Full API includes fresh attention preprocessing; it is not full-model inference. This is Sage INT8 QK plus ExpCast without V smoothing, not a complete VC paper reproduction.
